title: spec/rest: the query door's aggregation entry still strips an undeclared key, while MCP's aggregate_records now refuses it by name (#28550)
body:
domain:server#2 · os-project-manager · session_0186vfjHHMsRXC9EUT9hTFMo

Filing gate: ① out-of-scope finding from the #28550 dev (os-dev-report `6555058015`), answered by the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review on PR #28600 (comment `6555135229`, ③) as a legitimate follow-up and not a rider. Filed by `domain:server` seat 2. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets the grade.

Reach: any caller of `POST /data/:object/query` that sends an aggregation entry with a key the spec does not declare.
Reader who acts: `domain:server` (`packages/spec` `AggregationNodeSchema`, the REST query door).

## What happens

PR #28600 (#28550) makes the MCP tool `aggregate_records` take each aggregation entry as the spec's `AggregationNodeSchema` members, closed: an undeclared entry key (for example `bogusKey`, or `where` meant as `filter`) is refused by name. The REST query door parses the same entry with `AggregationNodeSchema`, which is a plain object, so it still strips an undeclared entry key and answers. After #28600 the two doors judge one entry shape differently: MCP refuses, REST strips. REST computes nothing wrong today (a stripped unknown key changes nothing it computes), so this is a consistency gap, not a wrong answer.

## Wanted

One strict contract at the producer: the aggregation entry refuses an undeclared key by name on every door that accepts it, in the same wording the unknown-key campaign uses (`strictUnknownKeyError`), with the retired `distinct` keeping its tombstone sentence. This is a spec narrowing, so the PR declares `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, and a contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is owed. Test: REST and MCP give one refusal for an undeclared entry key, and entries with only declared members answer as today on both.

Dedupe: searched `AggregationNodeSchema strict`; no open card.

Links back: #28550, PR #28600
